extracted.intended_audience: faculty, administrators, and grant writers at two-year/community colleges seeking external funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, locating funding, writing, reviewing, and submitting grant proposals specifically for two-year (community) colleges. Emphasizes matching problems to funders and practical steps before and after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify an important problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtaining funding requires identifying an important problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project should address an issue significant enough to merit external support; funders are selective and resources are limited, so the problem statement must justify why the work is necessary and worth funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate / find an appropriate funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: Locating an appropriate funding source is required to obtain funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the project to funders receptive to community colleges; use lists of institutions and publications (provided in the digest) to assist in locating suitable government agencies and private foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present the idea effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting the idea effectively is required to obtain funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, persuasive presentation increases competitiveness. Effective presentation encompasses organization, clarity of objectives, and convincing rationale that distinguishes the proposal from many worthwhile but unfunded submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning the project is an important step in writing a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a feasible work plan and timeline prior to writing; planning informs budget, staffing, methods, and demonstrates to reviewers that the project can be executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properly organize and write the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly organizing and writing the proposal is an essential step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conventional proposal structure and include required sections (the digest describes the 'four main elements of a proposal'); ensure logical flow, clear objectives, methods, and budget justification to aid reviewer comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the proposal for consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the proposal for consistency before submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for internal consistency among goals, methods, timeline, and budget; correct errors and ensure alignment of claims and requested resources to avoid undermining credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit the proposal (follow submission procedures/timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting the proposal is a required step in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to funder deadlines and submission procedures; timely and correctly formatted submissions are prerequisite to consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the four main elements of a proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The digest includes a description of the four main elements of a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and include each core element as described by the digest (the fact sheet provides the detailed descriptions); these elements form the backbone of a complete proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take steps if the proposal is not funded
rubrics_metrics.description: The digest outlines steps to take if the proposal is not funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to rejection by revising and resubmitting, seeking feedback, identifying alternate funders, or scaling the project; treating non-award as part of the funding process improves future success.
